abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel graph spectral theory for adaptive image representation that fundamentally transforms conventional Euclidean-based image analysis paradigms. Current methods rely on fixed basis functions that cannot capture the intrinsic manifold structure of natural images. We propose modeling image patches as signals on a weighted graph, where spectral properties of the graph Laplacian serve as adaptive basis functions for representation. The theoretical contribution establishes rigorous mathematical connections between graph spectral analysis and image characteristics including smoothness, sparsity, and edge discontinuities. We prove that the proposed graph spectral representation yields orthogonal, data-dependent basis functions that automatically adapt to local image structure without predetermined transforms. The framework provides a unified mathematical foundation bridging discrete graph representations and continuous image domains. Experimental validation on benchmark datasets demonstrates that the proposed theory achieves superior performance in image denoising, compression, and feature extraction tasks compared to state-of-the-art methods including DCT and wavelet-based approaches. This work establishes a new theoretical paradigm in image representation by providing a principled framework for data-adaptive signal decomposition on graphs.

This paper presents an optimized multi-scale transform theory that significantly advances wavelet-based image denoising performance. While wavelet transforms have been extensively applied to image denoising, conventional approaches suffer from fixed basis selections that inadequately handle diverse image structures across scales. We introduce a scale-space decomposition framework with theoretically optimal wavelet parameter selection based on local variance and gradient characteristics. The mathematical analysis derives that adaptively choosing wavelet parameters according to local content yields superior energy compaction compared to conventional fixed transforms. We establish rigorous bounds on the reconstruction error and prove that the optimized transform provides up to 3dB improvement in signal-to-noise ratio under sparse prior assumptions. The theoretical framework enables principled parameter selection that balances noise suppression and feature preservation. Extensive experiments on standard test images validate the theoretical predictions, demonstrating average PSNR improvements of 2.3dB over state-of-the-art wavelet denoising methods including BM3D. The proposed theory provides a principled approach to parameter optimization that significantly enhances practical denoising performance while maintaining theoretical rigor.

This paper proposes a novel end-to-end image compression system that fundamentally rethinks the architecture of learned image compression by introducing hierarchical context modeling. Unlike traditional block-based compression standards such as JPEG and HEVC, the proposed system learns the entire compression pipeline including transformation, quantization, and entropy coding from data in a unified framework. The key architectural innovation lies in the hierarchical context module that captures multi-scale dependencies across image regions, enabling more accurate probability estimation for arithmetic coding. The system employs a novel rate-distortion optimization strategy that learns to allocate bits based on perceptual quality metrics rather than pixel-level metrics. We design a convolutional network architecture with gated fusion mechanisms that effectively combines local and global context information. Experimental results on standard benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed system achieves 28% bitrate reduction compared to JPEG at equivalent perceptual quality assessed by LPIPS. For high-resolution images, the system outperforms BPG and WebP while maintaining practical computational complexity. This work presents a complete paradigm shift from hand-crafted compression standards to learned representations.

This paper presents an enhanced medical image segmentation system that substantially improves upon standard U-Net architectures through novel multi-scale attention mechanisms and boundary-aware training. While U-Net has achieved widespread adoption for medical image segmentation, existing implementations struggle with inconsistent performance across structures of varying scales and imprecise boundary delineation. The proposed system introduces a scale attention module that dynamically weights feature responses from different encoder levels based on their relevance to target structures. This attention mechanism particularly enhances small structure detection while suppressing noise in ambiguous regions. Additionally, we design a boundary-focused loss function that emphasizes pixel-level accuracy at organ and lesion boundaries, addressing the common issue of boundary blur. The architecture maintains computational efficiency comparable to standard U-Net through efficient feature fusion modules. Comprehensive evaluation on three medical imaging datasets including cardiac MRI, abdominal CT, and retinal OCT demonstrates consistent improvements. The system achieves average Dice coefficients of 0.94, 0.91, and 0.89 respectively, representing improvements of 4-7% over baseline U-Net variants. The proposed system provides a practical solution for clinical applications requiring accurate and efficient organ and lesion segmentation.
